chapter: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
title: The young man's happiest moment
summary: The student, studying agriculture in Wichita, says working with a Black classmate changed his mind about his family's views.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: The young man that had his dad fix it. I asked him what did he mean and he said well, as you see my dad's all right, but there's no negroes around this area at all and they had their own idea and naturally I was raised around them and I thought the same way, and I'm going to school now at the University of Wichita, he was taking agriculture, that's a big wheat area, and he was going for what everybody was doing there, and so he says
the first project they sent him out on, they sent a negro--

To work with him. And he just went swelling up then but he didn't say anything and finally he and this negro got acquainted, were good friends and he said I wouldn't have passed that first semester if it hadn't been for this negro, and when I came back home I told my people, you all are so wrong about colored people, you just don't know them and haven't been around them, they're just like anybody else, some are good and some are bad, just like anybody else. But to think that I could do something for you just makes me so happy.
